name: L'Oréal
summary: L'Oréal's careers site describes a CV screen, sometimes three short questions answered online to gauge cultural fit, a first call with a recruiter about your motivation and which division or role suits you, and a longer interview with your potential manager, typically 45 to 60 minutes. It suggests answering with the STARE method and giving examples where you took initiative or owned a project end to end. For junior roles it says the process usually takes about a month.
rounds: For some roles, three short online questions on cultural fit
First interview with a recruiter on motivation and fit, often about 30 minutes
Interview with your potential manager, often 45 to 60 minutes
Further interviews or a case for some roles, then an offer
looks_for: Initiative and ownership of projects end to end
Curiosity about the brands and markets

questions.text: Tell me about a project you owned from start to finish.
covers: What you did at each stage
The result and what you learned from it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took the initiative without being asked.
Tell me about a time you had to convince people with different opinions.
Tell me about a failure and what you'd do differently.
How would you launch a skincare product for a younger audience in a new market?
covers: Who they are and what they want

questions.text: Sales of a well-known brand are falling in one country. How would you find out why?
covers: Splitting by channel, product and customer

questions.text: How would you use social media data to choose which product to promote next month?
How would you make a product's packaging more sustainable without losing its appeal?
Which L'Oréal brand would you like to work on, and what would you change about it?
covers: One idea, grounded in what you've seen

questions.text: Pick a beauty trend you've noticed. What should a big company do about it?
covers: The trend and who's driving it

questions.text: Why do you want to work at L'Oréal?
covers: Something specific about L'Oréal or its brands
How your skills fit the role

questions.text: Which division or role suits you best, and why?

tips: L'Oréal suggests the STARE method for answers: situation, task, action, result and evaluation.
Prepare examples where you took initiative or owned a project end to end, as L'Oréal's careers site asks.
Know a few L'Oréal brands well, including how they're sold in your country.
L'Oréal says it never asks for sensitive personal information during recruitment; ignore suspicious messages.

sources.title: L'Oréal Careers: Apply to L'Oréal Groupe
